page: Amazon Web Services r8ib.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 480 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 512.0 GB of DDR5 running at 7 GHz, delivering an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network connectivity is rated at a 67 Gbps baseline. The configuration excludes onboard GPUs and contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for file persistence.

Benchmark metrics demonstrate strong multi-core throughput, recording 69185.74 in stress-ng tests despite average single-core performance. Memory subsystems achieve 192.87 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations and 5145.37 GB/sec for small cached blocks, while uncached write operations test in the average tier at 78.24 GB/sec. Supported hardware instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX assist compute tasks, achieving 439.84 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, 152.26 GB/sec in static web throughput, and 115.74 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. The system also sustains 292.47 tokens per second for prompt processing on 7B language models.

The absence of local disks shifts all I/O overhead to network storage, making external throughput considerations critical. However, the dedicated 67 Gbps interface and substantial DDR5 memory density provide solid resource efficiency for workloads constrained by RAM rather than disk latency. Amazon Web Services r8ib.16xlarge is technically matched to high-volume in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, real-time analytics pipelines, and CPU-focused inference services.
description: Amazon Web Services r8ib.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro system, powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. It features 32 physical cores, 64 dedicated vCPUs, 480 MB of L3 cache, and 512.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM allocation per core. The instance provides 67 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, lacks local ephemeral storage, and includes no discrete graphics processing units. Instruction support for AVX-512 and AMX contributes to high-tier multi-threaded decompression rates and strong prompt processing speeds for language models, while handling 115.74 million Redis SET operations per second. Although dependent on remote storage for persistent data, its dense memory profile and high networking throughput make it appropriate for memory-bound applications, including large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caches, and analytical batch processing.
